rawItems.title: Hunts man charged with seven counts of rape named for first time
rawItems.content: A man from Huntingdonshire charged with rape and intentional strangulation is due in court. Toby Tiller, of Princes Street, Ramsey, is due to appear at Huntingdon Magistrates' Court for his first hearing on Tuesday (November 17). He faces seven counts of raping a woman aged 16 years of age or older and two counts of intentional strangulation. The 24-year-old is also accused of engaging in controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate relationship. The alleged offences all said to have occurred in Cambridgeshire between August 2024 and May 2025. Have you got a story you want to share? A former Huntingdonshire NHS clinic could become a new later living development with up to 40 homes. Churchill Living is proposing to redevelop St Ives Clinic, the old NHS premises on Ramsey Road, into a later living development. The scheme would include around 38 one- and two-bedroom apartments and two cottages, all designed for people over 60. The site is brownfield, meaning it was previously developed but is now abandoned, vacant or underused. A spokesperson for Churchill Living said: "As we prepare to submit a formal planning application, we are keen to gather feedback and give local people the opportunity to have their say on our plans to regenerate this previously developed site in the heart of St Ives. "Delivering new homes in this well-connected location will help to regenerate this brownfield site and reduce the need for greenfield development to meet the urgent demand for new homes locally. "By giving older people in and around St Ives the option to downsize, it will also help release many larger, second-hand properties back onto the market for local families to move into, also creating opportunities for local first time buyers to get onto the ladder." rawItems.title: Motorcyclist seriously injured after crash involving Audi in Hunts town
rawItems.content: A motorcyclist has been seriously injured in a crash involving a car in a Huntingdonshire town. Police were called at 4.47pm on Saturday (November 14) to reports of a collision between an Audi Q3 and a motorbike in Great Whyte, Ramsey. Officers and paramedics attended and the motorcyclist was rushed to hospital with serious injuries, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. A spokesperson for the force said: "The Audi driver was unhurt and remained at the scene. "An investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information should contact us via the website or 101 quoting incident 360 of November 14." Have you got a story you want to share? rawItems.title: Environmental disaster fears after 14,000 litres of oil dumped in ditch off A14
rawItems.content: Calls for urgent action to avert an environmental disaster have been made after an estimated 14,000 litres of waste engine oil was dumped into a Huntingdonshire ditch. Robert Neilson has raised concerns after being alerted to the illegal 'fly-tipping' by a family member who farms the area off the A14 between the Leighton Bromswold and Catworth junctions. Mr Neilson, who lives in Ramsey, said his relative found the oil while working on the farm earlier this week. “He told me he contacted the Environment Agency straight away because he was so concerned about the amount of oil and the environmental disaster it could cause,” said Mr Neilson. items.title: Planning Committee Recommends Refusal for 25 Dwellings Off Oilmills Road
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting agenda 20261022): Unanimously recommended refusal for outline application 26/00142/OUT on grounds of highway safety on Oilmills Road, surface water flood risk, and overdevelopment beyond the settlement boundary.

items.title: Planning Committee Approves High Street Commercial Refurbishment & Signage
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting agenda 20261022): Supported planning application 26/00188/FUL for commercial shopfront renovation and heritage signage in the Ramsey Conservation Area.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Minutes 8 Oct 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.
